title: /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized returns unmapped_player for every player because the Sleeper block never contains the key the identity mapper is handed
claimUnderTest: server.py:11260 'Find this player's GSIS via the unified mapper, then filter.' The route's own comment says the row-filter bug was the defect and was fixed.
observed: players_dir = sleeper_block.get("players") or sleeper_block.get("playerDict"). The Sleeper block the scraper writes (Dynasty Scraper.py:1297-1306) contains exactly leagueId, leagueName, teams, positions, playerIds, idToPlayer, scoringSettings, rosterPositions, leagueSettings - no 'players', no 'playerDict', ever. players_dir is therefore always None, _index_directory(None) returns four empty dicts, resolve_player returns None, and the route short-circuits at reason: unmapped_player. Confirmed live on four real Sleeper ids (A.J. Brown 5859, Josh Allen 4984, Bijan Robinson 9509, Kenny Gainwell 7567): all four return unmapped_player. The stats fetch SUCCEEDS first (the route would otherwise say no_stats_available), so the mapper is the sole blocker. /api/status corroborates: idMappingCoverage = {resolve_attempts: 8, unresolved: 8, coverage_pct: 0.0}. This is a key-name mismatch in committed code, not container state.

reproduction.command: for sid in 5859 4984 9509 7567; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/player/$sid/realized"; echo; done
reproduction.expected: weekly realized-points arrays for each player

numericProof.formula: resolvable = |{sid : sleeper_block['players'] is a dict and sid in it}|

userImpact: PlayerPopup's realized-points panel is empty for every player in every league. A user comparing a player's market value against his actual production sees nothing and concludes there is no data.

priorFinding.note: A22-F03 claims the route 'emits a full array of 0.0-point weeks'; A22-F02 claims IDP players 'silently return zero weeks'. Neither reproduces: the route never reaches the scoring stage for ANY player. Both describe behaviour downstream of a bail that always fires. Same for PRIOR-A21-F16's league-scoping claim - the response never contains weeks to mis-score.

whatWorks: The route's auth gate, flag gate, league resolution and the nfl_data weekly fetch all work - the fetch returns rows, which is why the response is unmapped_player rather than no_stats_available.
rootCause: server.py reads sleeper.players / sleeper.playerDict; the producer emits sleeper.playerIds (name->id) and sleeper.idToPlayer (id->name). No writer has ever produced the key the reader asks for.
requiredRepair: Either fetch the Sleeper player directory for the mapper, or resolve the GSIS id from idToPlayer[sid] plus the nflverse name index. A key rename alone is NOT enough - playerIds/idToPlayer carry no gsis_id.
